subtopics.title: From Gross to Net — the Deductions

questions.question: A deduction is best described as:
options: The employer's extra expense on top of gross
The employee's own money, redirected from gross to an agreed destination
A voluntary gift to the state

questions.question: With PAYE, the employer acts as:
options: The owner of the tax money
The collector — deducting per the SARS tables and paying it over monthly

questions.question: The administrator's total deductions (PAYE 1 430, pension 825, UIF 110, medical 520, union 75) come to:
options: R2 960, leaving net pay of R8 040
R2 850, leaving net pay of R8 150
R3 060, leaving net pay of R7 940
R1 565, leaving net pay of R9 435

questions.question: Which pair of deductions is percentage-based rather than a fixed amount?
options: Pension (7,5% of gross) and UIF (1% of gross)

questions.question: A contribution differs from a deduction because it:
options: Is paid by the employer on top of gross and never shrinks net pay
Appears on the payslip as a subtraction

questions.question: The Skills Development Levy is unusual because:
options: It is deducted from the employee only
It has no employee half at all — a purely employer-side levy of 1% of gross, paid to SARS
It is paid to the union

questions.question: The administrator's total employer contributions (pension 825, UIF 110, medical 520, SDL 110) come to:
The total cost of employing the administrator is:
options: Her gross plus her own deductions
R12 565 — gross of R11 000 plus employer contributions of R1 565

subtopics.title: The Salaries Journal, the Wages Journal and the CPJ

questions.question: The amount credited to Bank through the CPJ for the administrator's pay is:
options: R8 040 — only the net leaves for her bank account

questions.question: The deductions withheld from gross are credited to:
options: Creditor accounts for SARS, the pension fund, the UIF, the medical scheme and the union — they are now owed

questions.question: The single payment to the pension fund after payday carries:
options: R1 650 — both halves, employee's deduction and employer's contribution
R825 plus the SDL of R110

questions.question: Ndlovu's Wages Journal row (gross R2 225, PAYE R222,50, UIF R22,25) shows net pay of:
Every payroll deduction is only legitimate when:
options: A written contract authorises it by signature
The employer decides it is fair

questions.question: The payroll signature of nepotism is:
options: A name earning outside the scale — appointed or promoted past better-qualified colleagues
Two workers on the same notch

questions.question: 'Correct books, wrong conduct' describes a payroll that:
options: Balances perfectly while recording unequal pay for equal responsibility

questions.question: The employer's duties toward the union subscription are to:
options: Add it to the employee's net pay
Deduct it faithfully, pay it over promptly, and respect the union's role

questions.question: The five stops the envelope makes are:
options: Tax office, retirement jar, just-in-case insurance, doctor cover, union
SARS, the bank, the landlord, the union, the shop

questions.question: The envelope that started at R11 000 arrives holding:
options: R8 040 — after R2 960 was redirected in the worker's name

questions.question: 'Nothing was taken FROM you at those stops' means:
options: Every rand that left was the worker's own money, sent ahead to agreed destinations

questions.question: The second envelope is filled with:
options: Money moved out of the worker's envelope
The employer's own contributions — matching pension, UIF and medical, plus the skills levy

questions.question: 'Save one, get one' describes:
options: The rand-for-rand pension match — the shop puts R825 beside the worker's R825

questions.question: The true monthly cost of the job is:
options: R12 565 — gross plus the second envelope's R1 565

questions.question: Mixing up the two envelopes collapses the sum because:
options: Deductions shrink the worker's envelope while contributions are extra on top — they must never cross
Both envelopes hold the same amounts
Contributions are subtracted from net pay
Deductions are paid by the employer

questions.question: The deal goes on paper before the first shift because:
options: Memory negotiates and paper does not — the paper is the worker's case if the envelope runs light

questions.question: A shop that hires the manager's nephew over a better candidate pays twice:
options: Once in tax and once in UIF
Once in the nephew's salary and once in his pension
Once in weaker work, and once in every good worker who stops trying or leaves
Once now and once at year end

questions.question: 'Balancing is not the same as being right' means:
options: Fair pay cannot be recorded in books
Books can record unfair pay in perfectly neat, balancing columns

questions.question: One worker asking for a fair rate is a request; every worker asking together is:
options: A negotiation — the union's collective voice at the table
